title: This startup is issuing AI-generated acne prescriptions
source_used: The Verge (full text from fulltext/C10-01.txt); it relays Nolla Health's announcement and cites Bloomberg
key_facts: Healthcare startup Nolla Health announced on Monday (5 Oct 2026) that users in Utah can scan their faces with its app, and its AI system rates acne severity and writes a prescription on its own; The Verge says Bloomberg reported this earlier.

It launches as a pilot with gradually loosening physician oversight: two physicians approve each AI-generated prescription before it is issued for the first 100 patients; for up to 500 patients they review prescriptions only after they are issued; after that physicians review a sample of at least 10% a month plus every case involving an escalation or side effect (Nolla Health).

Utah started allowing AI systems to renew certain medications earlier this year, and several other healthcare companies are experimenting with AI prescriptions there; Nolla Health says it is the first in the country to issue initial prescriptions rather than renewals.
The service costs $4.99 a month and applies only to Utah residents aged 18 or over with mild-to-moderate acne.
Nolla Health says it will direct users to a physician if the AI cannot confidently select a treatment; according to Bloomberg the AI can currently prescribe eight different skin treatments.
Nolla Health says the pilot is designed to complement, not replace, physicians, by handling routine low-acuity cases so dermatologists can focus on complex, high-risk patients.
The Verge's subhead says Utah has signed off on the system; no statement from the state was in the text read.
quote_evidence: People in Utah can now use AI to get a prescription for acne treatment.
But Nolla Health says it’s the first in the country to issue initial prescriptions, rather than renewals.
“The pilot is designed to complement, not replace, physicians,” Nolla Health writes in its press release.
why_it_matters_hint: A reported US first for AI writing first-time prescriptions, run as a small Utah pilot whose doctor checks ease as patient numbers grow.
notes: Credit chain: The Verge writes its own report from Nolla Health's press release (quoted) and says Bloomberg reported it earlier, citing Bloomberg for the eight treatments; the chain is not fully clear, so the entry reads 'The Verge, citing Nolla Health's announcement and an earlier Bloomberg report'. Utah's sign-off is The Verge's own statement. Pilot scale: one state, adults only, mild-to-moderate acne.
